title: River Village: Fisherman's Joy
medium: Fan painting mounted as album leaf; ink and color on silk

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund

source.label: Cleveland Museum of Art record: c. 1302–3
Cleveland Museum of Art: “this blue-green–style landscape”

highlight.text: The artist of this blue-green–style landscape, Zhao Mengfu, was a southerner, versed in all fields of literati pursuits, such as calligraphy and connoisseurship.

source.label: Cleveland Museum of Art: “a distinctively southern flat watery landscape”

work.text: This painting combines a distinctively southern flat watery landscape combined with features of the northern landscape tradition, notably the spiky trees, branches, and rough-surfaced rocks.

moment.text: A princeling of the defeated Southern Song dynasty, he was nevertheless successfully recruited by Khubilai Khan to the Mongol court in the new capital, Dadu (modern Beijing), in 1286.

matters.text: Chao Meng-fu may have been ever so skilful as a painter and a calligraphist, and a most able and upright official; yet, he could never become the ideal of the true scholars, … because he had submitted to foreign conquerors and chosen the easier path, which led to fame and success, but not to the shining glory of unyielding patriots.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: A History of Early Chinese Painting, vol. II
